reason: The original's multiplying fill swaps the middle two pixels of every group of four it processes together (an error in its MMX loop). The replacement writes each pixel in place.
Same multiplying fill as above, one row at every start and width; documents the original's pixel order.
The original corrupts an overlapping copy within one surface for this shift (bytes of neighbouring pixels are mixed). The replacement copies the pixels as they were before the call.
With clipping mode 0 the original writes outside the destination when the destination rectangle leaves it, which corrupts memory or faults. The replacement draws the part inside the destination.
A source rectangle outside the image makes the original read memory before or after the pixels, which changes from run to run. The replacement draws the part inside the image.
A negative source origin makes the original read memory before the pixels, which changes from run to run. The replacement copies the part inside the image.
A source rectangle outside the image makes the original read memory outside the pixels. The replacement draws the part inside the image.

With textures smaller than the screen the original writes outside them and corrupts its heap, so its pixels are not a reference. The suite checks that no flags value ends the game; screen-size copies are covered by original_sgl_oracle.
